# tuna_tls_certificate (Resource)

A custom TLS certificate uploaded to the team.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tuna_tls_certificate" "example" {
  description     = "wildcard for tunnels.example.com"
  certificate_pem = file("${path.module}/cert.pem")
  # Write-only: not stored in state, requires Terraform >= 1.11
  private_key_pem = file("${path.module}/key.pem")
}

resource "tuna_domain_zone" "example" {
  domain             = "tunnels.example.com"
  tls_certificate_id = tuna_tls_certificate.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `certificate_pem` (String) PEM-encoded certificate chain.
- `private_key_pem` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) PEM-encoded private key. Write-only: never stored in state, requires Terraform >= 1.11. Key rotation happens together with certificate_pem replacement.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (Number) The ID of this resource.
- `issuer_common_name` (String)
- `not_after` (String)
- `not_before` (String)
- `serial_number` (String)
- `subject_alternative_names` (List of String)
- `subject_common_name` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# After import, set private_key_pem in the configuration: the API never returns it
terraform import tuna_tls_certificate.example 123
```
